<p class="lx-eyebrow">A spatial layer</p><p>Your study adds wind-turbine locations from the U.S. Wind Turbine Database for Prairie Town's county (illustrative). The file stores latitude and longitude in degrees (<span class="lx-term" data-term="epsg-code">EPSG:4326</span>).</p><p>The projected options: <span class="lx-term" data-term="utm">UTM</span> zones keep distances close to true locally; <span class="lx-term" data-term="web-mercator">Web Mercator</span> is for showing web maps; <span class="lx-term" data-term="equal-area-projection">equal-area Albers</span> keeps areas true across the contiguous U.S.</p><ul>
<li>Which coordinate system for 1 km setback buffers (the zone within 1 km of each turbine)? Right: a local projected system in meters, such as the county's <span class="lx-term" data-term="utm">UTM</span> zone, keeps distances close to true.</li>
<li>And for the area the 1 km buffers cover, in square kilometers? Right: an equal-area system for the contiguous United States keeps areas true.</li>
</ul>

We removed outliers [2] and filled missing values [3], and converted times to local time [4]. Annual demand was about 299 TWh [5].</p><ol class="lx-ex-static"><li value="1"><b>Falls short:</b> Which form, area, files, download date and license? A reader cannot find the same file.</li><li value="2"><b>Falls short:</b> No rule and no count; and removing is not flagging: the hours vanish from every total.</li><li value="3"><b>Falls short:</b> EIA's adjusted file has no blanks: the gaps are the hours you flagged. Which method, and how many hours?</li><li value="4"><b>Falls short:</b> Which zone, and what happened to the 23- and 25-hour days?</li><li value="5"><b>Falls short:</b> Raw or cleaned? Here both round to 299 TWh (299.48 and 298.56), so only a log can say which.</li></ol></div>
<div class="lx-ex-ans good"><p class="lx-eyebrow">Strong answer · Proficient (audit trail)</p><p class="lx-ex-lines"><b>Source:</b> EIA Form EIA-930 six-month BALANCE files, balancing authority SWPP, 2025, accessed 2 November 2026, SHA-256 fac4bb99… and 1146158b… [1].
<b>Extraction:</b> EIA's adjusted columns; each fuel's columns summed, negative values set to 0 [2]; input file b02-python-data.json, SHA-256 54fb03b9… [3].
<b>License:</b> EIA data public domain, cited with the date; the course's extract CC BY 4.0, credited [4].
<b>Time:</b> rows kept in UTC, hour ending; results labeled in Central time with daylight saving [5].
<b>Spikes:</b> demand under half the median (16,541 MW): 1 hour, 21 June, 1,505 MW [6], flagged as implausible; to check against SPP's records.
<b>Frozen:</b> runs of 3 or more identical non-zero readings: demand 698 h, wind 671 h, solar 1,377 h [7]; suspected stuck feeds, as in the course's data build.
<b>Fill:</b> the same UTC hour on valid days within 7, 21 or 45 days, to keep the daily shape.
<b>Effect:</b> annual demand 298.56 TWh (raw 299.48); lowest hour 24.4 GW (raw 1.5) [8]; leaving the flagged hours out would give 275.09 TWh [9].
<b>Known limits:</b> 65 night hours still show solar above 5% of its peak, 49 of them filled; a night rule comes next [10].
<b>Rerun:</b> the starter notebook r04-data.ipynb, with these four settings, prints the four numbers [11].
<b>Validation:</b> not yet; studio R5 adds the verification log and a check against an independent source [12].</p><ol class="lx-ex-static"><li value="1"><b>Works:</b> Date and checksums let anyone confirm they downloaded the same EIA files.</li><li value="2"><b>Works:</b> Even an extract changes values: the clipping belongs in the audit trail.</li><li value="3"><b>Works:</b> The extract itself, by its own checksum: the exact file this note's cleaning starts from.</li><li value="4"><b>Works:</b> Two layers of terms: the government data, and the course's extract of it.</li><li value="5"><b>Works:</b> No hour is lost or doubled, and every clock time on the page is named.</li><li value="6"><b>Works:</b> Rule, threshold, count and the value itself.</li><li value="7"><b>Works:</b> Counts per column, so the reader sees what each rule flagged.</li><li value="8"><b>Works:</b> Raw against cleaned: the reader sees what cleaning changed.</li><li value="9"><b>Works:</b> The rejected alternative and its effect: the choice is defended, not just made.</li><li value="10"><b>Works:</b> A check the rules fail, reported rather than hidden.</li><li value="11"><b>Works:</b> Anyone can rebuild the numbers from the note and one file.</li><li value="12"><b>Works:</b> Proficient for R4's part, the audit trail: the rubric's verification log and validation come in R5.</li></ol></div>
</div>
<table class="lx-facts lx-ex-diff"><thead><tr><th scope="col"></th><th scope="col">Weak answer</th><th scope="col">Strong answer</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><th scope="row">Provenance</th><td>“EIA”</td><td>Form, area, year, access date, checksums, extraction, license</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Each step</th><td>A verb</td><td>Rule, threshold, count, and a flag called provisional</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Effect</th><td>One rounded number</td><td>Raw against cleaned, and the rejected alternative</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Limits and rerun</th><td>None</td><td>A failed check reported; a notebook that rebuilds the numbers</td></tr></tbody></table>
<!-- r04-exemplars:end -->
<dl class="lx-ideas">
<dt>Defend, not just clean</dt><dd>For each step: the rule, the count, the reason, and what the result would be with the alternative.</dd>
<dt>Flag, then fill</dt><dd>Never delete silently: flag by a stated rule, then fill or leave out, and log which. A flag is a suspicion until other evidence confirms it.</dd>
<dt>Check the result</dt><dd>Run a check the rules did not make, such as solar at night, and log what still fails.</dd>
<dt>Time</dt><dd>Keep the rows as published (UTC, hour ending) and change only the labels.</dd>
<dt>Licenses</dt><dd>Public domain still asks for a citation. Share-alike terms can differ for a database you derive and for a map made from it: check which apply to your output.</dd>
</dl>
</div>
</div>

```{=html}
<div class="lx-deepers">
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper</span>Why this page does not fill demand from the forecast</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
<p>The course's own data build fills flagged demand hours from SPP's day-ahead forecast, rescaled to the demand around each gap, which gives a lowest hour of 23.7 GW.</p>
<p>This raw file carries no forecast column, so here every column uses the same-hour rule, which gives 24.4 GW.</p>
<p>Two defensible fills, two answers: that difference belongs in the note.</p>
</div>
</details>
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper</span>What this studio leaves out</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
<ul>
<li>Metadata standards and data papers: the FAIR principles (findable, accessible, interoperable, reusable) ask that machines, not only people, can find and read your data.</li>
<li>Personal data: meter readings, survey answers and addresses need consent and protection before any cleaning (<a href="r09-integrity-stakeholders.html">R9</a>).</li>
<li>Revisions: agencies revise past data; the access date and checksums in your note are what make a revision visible.</li>
</ul>
</div>
</details>
</div>

<tr><td class="n">B2's notebook</td><td>Loading, checking and plotting the same file, with the night rule; it also needs <a href="../assets/learn/data/town_year.json">town_year.json</a>.</td><td class="s"><a href="notebooks/b02-python-data.ipynb">.ipynb</a></td></tr>
<tr><td class="n">QGIS</td><td>Free desktop GIS for the spatial practice: reproject, buffer, measure areas.</td><td class="s"><a href="https://qgis.org/">qgis.org</a></td></tr>
<tr><td class="n">EIA-930 six-month files</td><td>The source files, with their checksums in the JSON's metadata.</td><td class="s"><a href="https://www.eia.gov/electricity/gridmonitor/dashboard/electric_overview/US48/US48">EIA Grid Monitor</a>, Download Data → Six-Month Files · as of 2 November 2026</td></tr>
<tr><td class="n">U.S. Wind Turbine Database</td><td>Turbine locations for the spatial step; public domain, acknowledgment requested.</td><td class="s"><a href="https://energy.usgs.gov/uswtdb/">usgs.gov</a> · v9.1, checked 3 November 2026</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
